acceptance_criteria.criterion: The `QueueEntry` interface in `types.ts` includes a `projectExists: boolean` field.
`getQueue()` populates `projectExists` from `projectStatus.exists` for every returned entry.
The "View Project" button is NOT rendered when `projectExists` is `false`, even if `effectiveStatus === 'started'`.
The "View Project" button IS rendered when `projectExists` is `true` and `entry.expectedSlug` is truthy.
A unit test covers both the `projectExists: true` and `projectExists: false` cases for `getQueue()` output.
Existing tests continue to pass without modification (no regressions).

summary: All WP-005 deliverables were already present in the codebase: (1) `QueueEntry` in `types.ts` includes `projectExists: boolean` with JSDoc; (2) `getQueue()` in `get-queue.ts` populates `projectExists` from `projectStatus.exists`; (3) `orchestrator.js` gates the "View Project" button on `entry.projectExists === true && entry.expectedSlug`; (4) `get-queue.test.ts` covers both `projectExists: true` and `projectExists: false` cases. Full test suite (2201 tests, 73 files) passes with zero failures.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified against source code and live test execution.
AC-1 PASS: `QueueEntry` interface in types.ts (line 87) declares `projectExists: boolean` with clear JSDoc documenting its purpose and relationship to `getProjectLedgerStatus().exists`.
AC-2 PASS: `getQueue()` in get-queue.ts (line 160) destructures `{ exists: projectExists }` from the `getProjectLedgerStatus()` result and assigns it directly to the `QueueEntry` object (line 177).

AC-3 PASS: orchestrator.js button-rendering block (lines 268-291) uses the branch `entry.projectExists === true && entry.expectedSlug` — `View Project` is only rendered when both conditions are true. No path from `projectExists: false` can reach the button rendering code.
AC-4 PASS: The same conditional at line 285 confirms the button renders when `projectExists === true` and `entry.expectedSlug` is truthy. `encodeURIComponent` is applied to the slug in the href.

AC-5 PASS: get-queue.test.ts contains two dedicated `describe` blocks — one for `projectExists: true` (creates ledger on disk) and one for `projectExists: false` (no ledger created). Both cases assert on `entries[0].projectExists`.
AC-6 PASS: Full test suite — 73 files, 2201 tests — executes with zero failures (exit code 0).

metrics.test_coverage: Both projectExists:true and projectExists:false branches explicitly exercised in get-queue.test.ts

comments.note: Edge-case: `effectiveStatus === 'started'` with `projectExists === false` is structurally impossible — `computeEffectiveStatus()` returns 'started' only when `projectExists` is true (line 45). The AC-3 guard in orchestrator.js is therefore belt-and-suspenders, which is correct defensive practice.

Edge-case: `isRawQueueEntry()` does not reject `expectedSlug: ''` (only validates `typeof === 'string'`). An empty-slug entry would enter the queue with `projectExists: false` and the button guard `entry.projectExists === true && entry.expectedSlug` correctly suppresses the View Project link. No regression introduced by this WP; pre-existing gap worth tracking.
URL safety: `encodeURIComponent(entry.expectedSlug)` applied on orchestrator.js line 287 ensures slugs with special characters produce valid hrefs. Verified.

summary: Code review PASS across all four modified files. The projectExists field is introduced cleanly and consistently: strongly typed in types.ts with authoritative JSDoc that explicitly steers callers away from heuristic effectiveStatus inference; populated fail-safely via destructuring alias in get-queue.ts; guarded with strict equality (=== true) plus truthy-slug check in orchestrator.js; covered in two focused, well-isolated test cases in get-queue.test.ts.

Maintainability: Excellent. All identifiers are descriptive, the dependency chain comment at the top of types.ts is current and accurate, and the priority-comment block in orchestrator.js makes branching intent immediately clear.
Best practices: DRY and SOLID principles followed. getProjectLedgerStatus is fail-safe and single-responsibility. Promise.all usage in getQueue is correct for concurrent I/O. No over-engineering.
Performance: No concerns. The only I/O path added (ledger file stat) is already parallelised with the existing resolveProgress call via Promise.all.
Technical debt: The pre-existing empty-slug gap in isRawQueueEntry() (noted by QA) is not introduced by this WP and is correctly handled by the existing UI guard. Tagged for Documentation.

comments.note: types.ts line 55: The @remarks pre-reference to projectExists in the class-level JSDoc (before the field declaration at line 87) is a deliberate self-documentation pattern — it makes the intent of the field discoverable at the interface level without having to find the field declaration. Excellent practice.
get-queue.ts lines 153-158: Promise.all([getProjectLedgerStatus, resolveProgress]) correctly parallelises the two independent async I/O operations per entry. No serial await antipattern present.

orchestrator.js line 285: Using strict equality `entry.projectExists === true` (rather than just truthy) is the correct choice given the field is typed boolean — it guards against accidental truthiness from undefined or other non-boolean values that could appear in the JS runtime from a deserialized API response.

compute-effective-status.ts line 45: Rule 1 (`if (projectExists) return 'started'`) confirms the QA finding — `effectiveStatus === 'started'` with `projectExists === false` is structurally impossible. The AC-3 UI guard is belt-and-suspenders, which is correct defensive practice.

[documentation-forward] isRawQueueEntry() in get-queue.ts validates `typeof e['expectedSlug'] === 'string'` but does not reject empty strings. An empty-slug entry enters the queue with projectExists: false and the UI guard `entry.projectExists === true && entry.expectedSlug` correctly suppresses the View Project link. This is a pre-existing gap (not introduced by this WP) — worth a brief inline comment on isRawQueueEntry() noting the empty-slug behavior is handled by the UI layer rather than the validator.
